scope: Completed TREC repetition 1 control source and all eight stored prediction sets. Independent NumPy classification point losses only; original bootstrap outputs retained, not rerun. No candidate execution, checkpoint deserialization, model request or GPU execution. Full campaign is still running.

model_authored_rationales.b0-s0:
TREC question-type classification: feature-engineered sparse ensemble.

Rationale (exploratory, validated by group-aware CV on training rows only):
The common reference is a single word 1-2gram TF-IDF LinearSVC (dev error .134).
Three cheap, orthogonal sources of signal are added:

1. Explicit head-of-question features. TREC coarse classes are largely decided by
   the leading wh-phrase ("what is", "who", "how many", "where"). Bag-of-ngrams
   dilutes position, so the first/second/third leading tokens are appended as
   dedicated tokens (fwxq_/fw2xq_/fw3xq_) before word vectorization.
2. A char_wb 2-5 gram block (weighted .7) concatenated to the word block, which
   is robust to morphology/typos and to the small (3815 row) training set.
3. A heterogeneous classifier ensemble (RBF-SVM, two LinearSVCs, logistic
   regression, ComplementNB) combined by greedy weight selection with
   replacement on out-of-fold probabilities, so the combination is chosen by a
   grouped CV estimate rather than by authored belief.

Optionally, confident pseudo-labels on the unlabeled development features are
added to the training pool; this is *accepted only if* a held-out fold check
(train on folds 1..k-1, pseudo-label the unlabeled pool, refit, score fold 0)
shows a non-trivial gain. No development labels are read anywhere.

Limitations: CV is computed on training groups only and may be optimistic or
pessimistic relative to the disjoint development/audit groups; the pseudo-label
decision rests on a single fold split and is therefore noisy (it is gated by a
margin so that ties keep the simpler supervised model).
model_authored_rationales.b0-s1:
TREC question-type classification: sparse linear/NB ensemble blended with a
randomly-initialised word-CNN ensemble.

Rationale (exploratory; validated only by group-aware CV on training rows):
The common reference is a word 1-2gram TF-IDF LinearSVC (dev error .134) and the
previous branch step reached dev .119 with a purely sparse ensemble, which did
not qualify on the fresh confirmation split.  The remaining error of sparse
bag-of-ngram models on TREC is dominated by questions whose class depends on
short *ordered* phrases ("what is the name of", "how far", "what does X stand
for") that TF-IDF dilutes.  A Kim-style convolutional network over randomly
initialised word embeddings models exactly those local ordered patterns and is
a genuinely different hypothesis class, so its errors are largely decorrelated
from the sparse block; literature reports CNN-rand as clearly stronger than
linear bag-of-ngrams on TREC even without any pretrained vectors (none are
available here).

Design:
1. Sparse block: word 1-2grams (with explicit leading-token features) + char_wb
   2-5grams, four cheap learners (2 LinearSVC, logistic regression,
   ComplementNB) combined by greedy weight selection on grouped out-of-fold
   probabilities.
2. Neural block: word-CNN (embedding 128, filters 2/3/4/5 x 128, max-pool,
   dropout .5, word-dropout augmentation), averaged over several seeds.
3. Blend weight alpha chosen on the same grouped out-of-fold predictions by a
   coarse grid search, then both blocks refit on all labelled rows.

Limitations: all internal estimates use training groups only; development,
confirmation and audit groups are disjoint, so the CV numbers are proxies and
not measurements on the evaluated splits.  Seed averaging reduces but does not
remove neural variance; no development labels are read anywhere.
model_authored_rationales.b0-s2:
TREC question-type classification: calibrated, feature-diverse ensemble.

Rationale (exploratory; internal estimates use grouped CV on training rows only).
The common reference is a word 1-2gram TF-IDF LinearSVC (dev error .134).  The
previous branch step (sparse greedy ensemble) reached dev .119 -- an ~11%
relative reduction that did not survive the fresh confirmation split, i.e. the
margin was too thin.  Three changes aim at a wider, more stable margin rather
than at a new hypothesis about TREC itself:

1. Richer question-shape features.  Besides the leading 1/2/3 tokens (which
   carry most of the coarse-class signal), the final token, a length bucket,
   a digit flag and an internal-capitalisation flag (proper nouns -> ENTY/HUM/
   LOC) are appended as dedicated tokens before word vectorization.
2. Genuinely different hypothesis classes added to the sparse block: an NBSVM
   (one-vs-rest log-count-ratio weighted binary 1-3grams, a strong small-data
   text baseline) and a seed-averaged MLP over a truncated-SVD projection of
   the TF-IDF space (dense, non-linear, decorrelated errors).
3. Per-model temperature calibration of decision values by out-of-fold log
   loss before greedy weight selection.  Uncalibrated margins let one
   overconfident member dominate the average; calibrating first makes the
   combination closer to a proper probability average and reduces variance.

All combination weights and temperatures are chosen on grouped out-of-fold
predictions; the whole system is then refit on all labelled rows.  No
development labels are read anywhere.

Limitations: CV uses training groups only, while development/confirmation/audit
groups are disjoint, so CV numbers are proxies (observed to be pessimistic by
~3 points relative to development) and not measurements on evaluated splits.
Temperatures and blend weights are selected on the same out-of-fold matrix used
to report cv accuracy, so that figure is mildly optimistic.  MLP seed averaging
reduces but does not remove neural variance.
model_authored_rationales.b1-s0:
TREC topic classification: stronger sparse-feature ensemble over the LinearSVC reference.

Rationale (exploratory but grounded in standard TREC practice):
  * The reference uses only word 1-2gram TF-IDF + LinearSVC (dev error 0.1340).
    TREC question type is largely determined by the leading wh-phrase and by
    sub-word morphology of the head noun, so we add two extra feature blocks:
      (a) character n-grams (char_wb 2-5), robust to morphology/typos;
      (b) explicit positional "prefix" tokens (first three tokens, first
          bigram/trigram and the last token) which encode question-form cues
          that plain bag-of-ngrams dilutes.
  * Block weights, the linear-SVM regularisation strength and the classifier
    ensemble (LinearSVC / logistic regression / ComplementNB score averaging)
    are selected by GroupKFold cross-validation on the provided training
    groups, i.e. the declared generalization protocol, never on development
    labels (none are supplied to a method).
  * Scores of different members are z-normalised before averaging so that
    margin-based and probabilistic members contribute comparably.

Limitations: model selection uses ~3.8k training rows, so CV differences below
roughly 0.5 points are within noise; the reported CV numbers are in-training
estimates, not independent confirmations.
model_authored_rationales.b1-s1:
TREC question-type classification: diverse multi-family soft-vote ensemble.

Rationale (exploratory, validated only by GroupKFold CV on training rows):
  * The common reference is a single word 1-2gram TF-IDF LinearSVC.  A previous
    branch step showed that *selecting* one tweaked sparse-linear configuration
    by CV did not transfer to development (CV -1.5pt, dev +0.1pt), which is what
    one expects when CV differences (~0.6pt s.e.) are used for greedy selection.
    So here the emphasis is variance reduction by *averaging* structurally
    different learners instead of picking the CV winner.
  * Feature space: word 1-2gram TF-IDF + char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF (morphology of
    the head noun) + explicit positional "prefix" tokens (first tokens, leading
    bigram/trigram, last token) which carry the wh-form cue.  Vectorizer
    vocabularies/IDF are fit on train+development *texts only* (unsupervised,
    no labels), improving coverage for both evaluated splits.
  * Members: LinearSVC (C=1,4), multinomial logistic regression, ComplementNB,
    RBF-kernel SVC (non-linear on cosine-normalised TF-IDF), an NB-SVM
    (log-count-ratio scaled binary features, one-vs-rest), and a small sparse
    MLP trained on GPU (3 seeds averaged) - three genuinely different inductive
    biases plus two margin models.
  * Scores are row-centred and rescaled by an out-of-fold standard deviation so
    margins and log-probabilities contribute comparably; members clearly worse
    than the best member in CV are dropped; the weight vector is chosen among
    three fixed candidates by out-of-fold error.

Limitations: all model choices rest on 5-fold GroupKFold CV over 3815 training
rows (~0.6pt s.e.); no development labels are used or available to a method;
the CV estimate is mildly optimistic because vectorizers are fit once on all
unlabeled text.  Gains below ~1pt on development cannot be distinguished from
noise at these split sizes.
model_authored_rationales.b1-s2:
TREC question-type classification: variance-reduced multi-family, multi-view soft-vote ensemble.

Rationale (exploratory; validated only by GroupKFold CV on training rows):
  * Parent lineage (b1-s1) showed that *averaging* structurally different sparse
    learners beats CV-greedy selection of a single tweaked LinearSVC
    (dev 0.1181 vs reference 0.1340).  The remaining, easily removable source of
    variance in that recipe is the single arbitrary feature-block weighting
    (char 0.6 / prefix 0.8): the ensemble sees one view only.
  * This step keeps every ingredient that worked (word 1-2gram TF-IDF, char_wb
    2-5gram TF-IDF, positional "prefix" tokens for the wh-form cue, binary
    counts for NB-SVM; members LinearSVC C=1/4, multinomial LR, RBF-SVC,
    NB-SVM, sparse GPU MLP with several seeds) and adds a *second feature view*
    (char 1.0 / prefix 0.4) on which the two margin models are refit.  Feature
    view bagging averages away the block-weight choice instead of selecting it.
  * ComplementNB is dropped: in the parent OOF it was 9pt worse than the best
    member and was always filtered out, so its fit time is spent on extra MLP
    seeds instead.
  * Member scores are row-centred and rescaled by their out-of-fold standard
    deviation so margins and log-probabilities are commensurate; members more
    than 5pt worse than the best member in OOF are dropped; the weight vector is
    chosen among three fixed candidates by out-of-fold error (a 3-way choice,
    much less noisy than per-hyperparameter selection).
  * Vectorizer vocabularies/IDF are fit on train+development *texts only*
    (unsupervised, no labels are available to a method) for coverage.

Limitations: all choices rest on 5-fold GroupKFold CV over 3815 training rows
(s.e. ~0.6pt), so member ranking and the weighting choice are noisy; the CV
estimate is mildly optimistic because vectorizers are fit once on all unlabeled
text; no development or audit labels were used or measured here; differences
below ~1pt on development cannot be distinguished from noise at these sizes.

b0-s0.limitations: CV uses training groups only; development/audit groups are disjoint so these numbers are proxies, not measurements on the evaluated splits. The pseudo-label gate rests on one fold split and is noisy.

b0-s1.limitations: CV uses training groups only; development/confirmation/audit groups are disjoint, so these are proxies rather than measurements on evaluated splits. The blend weight is selected on the same out-of-fold matrix used to score it, so cv_accuracy_blend is mildly optimistic. CNN seeds add variance not captured by a single CV pass.

b0-s2.limitations: CV uses training groups only; development/confirmation/audit groups are disjoint, so these are proxies rather than measurements on the evaluated splits (the previous step observed CV error ~.149 with dev error ~.119). Temperatures and blend weights are selected on the same out-of-fold matrix that is scored, so cv_accuracy_ensemble is mildly optimistic. MLP seed averaging leaves residual neural variance.

b1-s0.limitations: CV differences below ~0.005 are within noise at this sample size; vectorizers were fit on the full training text (unsupervised) before CV, which is mildly optimistic for vocabulary coverage; no development labels used.

b1-s1.limitations: CV s.e. ~0.6pt on 3815 rows, so member ranking and the weighting choice among three fixed candidates are noisy; vectorizers were fit once on all unlabeled train+development text (no labels), mildly optimistic for vocabulary coverage; no development labels were used; development/audit performance is not measured here.

b1-s2.limitations: CV s.e. ~0.6pt on 3815 rows, so member ranking and the 3-way weighting choice are noisy; vectorizers fit once on all unlabeled train+development text (no labels), mildly optimistic for vocabulary coverage; two feature views are averaged rather than selected, but the view definitions themselves are fixed a priori and untested individually on held-out data; development/audit performance is not measured here.

review_findings: Control explored neural and NB-SVM methods; its failure does not show an absence of method diversity.
b0-s1 internally scored its CNN worse than the sparse ensemble and chose CNN weight zero. Final CNN count is zero; its development predictions exactly equal b0-s0.

Selected b1-s1 fits an MLP and NB-SVM alongside sparse models and uses them with nonzero final weights. Its selected OOF ensemble error 0.15963 is worse than the best individual OOF member 0.1536; the three weight candidates do not include a single-member fallback. This is an internal selection diagnostic, not proof that changing it would pass the external audit.

Selected audit has 47 errors versus the reference 50: 6% gain, below 10%, and its paired bootstrap upper difference is positive. Six valid paid attempts do not establish useful research progress by themselves.

The candidate passes both TREC repetitions with different methods (subword BiGRU mixture and semantic lexicon features). This is local success, not a causal attribution to any one method, an isolated method ablation or proof of generic creativity.
